result:
The full suite compiled cleanly and ran 82 tests with 1 failure. I verified the failure against the `Validate` source: in `noNullElements(Iterable, String, Object...)`, the `AtomicInteger` counter is only incremented when a null element is found (inside the `getAndIncrement()` call used to build the exception), never for the non-null elements that precede it. So the reported index is always `0` for whichever null is found first, not its real position — unlike the array overload, which correctly uses the loop index `i`. This contradicts the documented behavior ("the iteration index of the invalid element is appended").

**Bug found:** `testNoNullElementsIterable_withNullElementThrowsIAE_withIndex` fails because `Validate.noNullElements(Iterable, String, Object...)` reports index `0` instead of the element's actual index (`1`) when a null is found past the first position — the position counter isn't incremented for non-null elements it skips over.

All other 81 tests pass. The test class is at `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ValidateAgentTest.java`, self-contained (JUnit 5, no imports of other test files, Java 8-compatible syntax with anonymous `Executable` classes instead of lambdas).
